Same field at two detail levels; A is the more precise statement the document fully supports.

rulings.correct_value: eligible trials had to last at least 12 months; the 17 included studies lasted 18 to 27 months, with data analysed at 12, 18, 24 and above 24 months and the main results reported at 18 months
rulings.quote: The studies were conducted between 2014 and 2024, with durations varying from 18 months to 27 months.
rulings.reasoning: Reading B restates the inclusion threshold ('We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that lasted at least 12 months'), while reading A describes the actual durations and analysis time points ('We analysed data at 12, 18, 24, and over 24 months of treatment'; 'Below, we report the results of the studies at 18 months'). Both are in the document; A is the more precise and complete description.

rulings.quote: The intervention results in little or no difference in the absolute risk of ARIA‐H, compared with placebo at 24 months (RR 1.27, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.70; I² = 0%; ARD 17 more events/1000 participants, 95% CI 2 fewer to 43 more; 2 studies, 913 participants; high‐certainty evidence; Analysis 4.8)

notes: Total-versus-analysed participants: the review included 17 studies with 20,342 participants, but no single pooled analysis uses that denominator. The 18-month analyses cited here rest on much smaller subsets (e.g. ADAS-Cog 13 studies/9895; any ARIA E 11 studies/13,595; symptomatic ARIA E 2 studies/3522; symptomatic ARIA H 1 study/1795; SAEs 9 studies/11,904; mortality 7 studies/9733). Any record field should keep these distinct.
Symptomatic ARIA H at 18 months comes from a single RCT (1795 participants), so describing it as a 'pooled' estimate (reading B) is a misnomer even though the numbers are right.

Any ARIA H at 18 months was NOT pooled: I² = 81% prevented meta-analysis and the three study-level results are reported individually (RR 2.31; RR 1.91; RR 0.85). A downstream record should not report a pooled 18-month ARIA H effect.
Symptomatic brain haemorrhage was a prespecified critical outcome but was not reported by any study — the correct value for that harm is genuinely 'not reported', unlike ARIA E, ARIA H and mortality.

The comparator and follow-up conflicts both pit an eligibility criterion against what the included trials actually did; maintainers may want separate fields for 'eligibility criterion' and 'as-included characteristic' to stop this recurring.
